Confidence is not high because no candidate here provides clearly comparable PRS-only AUROC/R² across the leading contenders, and several models are near-tied on limited effect-size reporting.

Both candidates are direct matches to otosclerosis (trait_efo=otosclerosis). PGS001255 provides more PRS-comparable performance evidence, including PGS-only AUROC (0.6319) and PGS R² (no covariates)=0.01341 plus incremental AUROC, enabling a clearer assessment of PRS contribution and a heritability-ceiling sanity check (PGS-only R² well below the provided h2_obs=0.0048, noting scale differences but no obvious ceiling violation). PGS002046 reports only partial correlation (partial-r=0.0182) and lacks AUROC/R², making cross-model comparability weaker despite a larger variant count and training sample. Limitation: both models come from UK Biobank framework/portability-style publications rather than a disease-focused multi-cohort otosclerosis study, and PGS001255 uses a time-to-event phenotype (TTE otosclerosis), which is a mild endpoint mismatch for generic disease risk; these factors prevent a high-confidence, high-quality designation.

Direct-match candidates are present (multiple ovarian cancer / epithelial ovarian cancer / malignant neoplasm of ovary models). PGS000082 is best supported overall because it has strong endpoint fidelity to the target (incident ovarian cancer; trait_efo ovarian carcinoma), is evaluated in Europeans, and is backed by a large, disease-focused multi-cohort context with a comparatively higher reported discrimination among the broadly comparable ovarian-cancer models shown (full-model AUROC/C-index ~0.655–0.656). However, confidence is limited because the reported AUROC/C-index is a full-model metric with substantial non-genetic covariates (including family history and reproductive/hormonal factors), and no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, making cross-model PRS-only comparability uncertain; additionally, several other direct ovarian cancer models show similar effect-size evidence and/or different endpoint subtypes, so the superiority is not unequivocal from the visible metadata alone.

All 11 candidates are direct matches to pancreatic cancer/carcinoma (mostly EFO: exocrine pancreatic carcinoma; one PDAC-specific model). Among the broadly aligned pancreatic cancer models, PGS000083 has strong endpoint fidelity (incident pancreatic cancer), large European evaluation (n=391,491), and supportive effect-size evidence (HR=1.49, 95% CI 1.36–1.62) with consistent discrimination reported (AUROC 0.745; C-index ~0.742). Competing candidates either show weaker reported discrimination in comparable settings (e.g., PGS000385/PGS000386 AUROC ~0.58; PGS000725 AUROC ~0.64; PGS000663 AUROC 0.67 with much smaller validation n=956) or have notable comparability concerns: PGS002264 reports a higher AUROC (0.83) but is PDAC-specific and explicitly integrates diabetes/clinical risk covariates, making the full-model AUROC less informative for standalone PRS quality. A key limitation is that across the pool, reported AUROCs appear to be full-model metrics with covariates (no clear PGS-only AUROC/R2), so the apparent performance advantage cannot be cleanly attributed to the PRS alone, lowering confidence.

All 11 candidates are direct matches at the trait level (Parkinson’s disease), but several are progression/dementia endpoints (PGS000056 cognitive decline, PGS000211 motor decline, PGS000777 Parkinson’s disease dementia) rather than generic PD risk/status, making them weaker matches for the target trait as stated. Among the models with a direct PD diagnosis endpoint, PGS000903 (Lancet Neurol 2021 meta-analysis) has strong disease-focused multi-cohort development, a polygenic C+T construction with substantially more variants (1805) than the GWAS-hit-only scores, and the most informative visible performance evidence in this context (reported R²=0.054 and OR=6.25 for top vs bottom quartile; full-model AUROC=0.692), with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). However, confidence is not high because the reported AUROC appears to be full-model (not explicitly PGS-only), and other direct PD models also report full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS001774 AUROC=0.8 but with heavier covariates including family history and multiple risk factors, making that metric less PRS-comparable).

All four candidates are direct/near-direct matches to the target concept (peripheral vascular disease), with two labeled as peripheral vascular disease unspecified (PGS001843, PGS002055) and two as peripheral artery disease (PGS005158, PGS005217), which is a closely aligned vascular subtype. PGS005217 is best supported because it is disease-focused on incident peripheral artery disease, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant count (1,296,292), has broad multi-ancestry evaluation, and reports a strong PRS effect size (HR 1.66 per SD) alongside a concordance statistic (C-index 0.731). The main limitation is phenotype alignment ambiguity versus the target’s broader label (peripheral vascular disease vs peripheral artery disease) and the lack of clearly PRS-only AUC/R2 metrics across the candidate set (the portability models report only small partial correlations; the disease-focused model reports full-model discrimination/effect size but not PRS-only AUC/R2), preventing a high-confidence, metric-comparable winner.

All three candidates are direct-match on concept via trait_efo=preeclampsia, but endpoint fidelity differs. PGS003586 is the most phenotype-aligned: trait_reported is Pre-eclampsia and phenotyping_reported is Pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, matching the target best. It also comes from a disease-focused Nat Med study on preeclampsia/gestational hypertension with basic covariates (maternal age, age^2, PCs) and shows a moderate per-SD effect size (OR=1.31, 95% CI 1.24–1.38), stronger than the gestational-hypertension-labeled sibling PGS003587 (OR=1.20). PGS004593 has a surface label match (Preeclampsia) and large validation size, but its phenotyping_reported is gestational hypertension (a mismatch for the target) and it reports HR=1.16, suggesting weaker PRS signal; training details are also listed as N/A/empty. Confidence is not high because none of the models report PRS-comparable AUC/R2, and there is some phenotype-field inconsistency across candidates (notably PGS003587 and PGS004593).

Multiple direct-match prostate cancer PRS candidates are present. PGS004155 is preferred because it has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: "Prostate cancer"), reports comparatively strong discrimination in a setting with no added covariates (covariates: "0"), and comes from a disease-specific benchmarking context with large external evaluation (validation_sample_size n=171,474; AUROC 0.7049 with accompanying R² 0.128). Competing candidates either (a) use horizon-conditioned/absolute-risk packaging (e.g., 5-year incident risk models such as PGS005237–PGS005241), which domain guidance flags as a negative for standalone PRS quality/comparability, (b) are pan-trait/framework-derived (e.g., PGS001291 snpnet across 813 traits), which is penalized when strong disease-focused alternatives exist, or (c) have less comparable or weaker/more covariate-inflated performance evidence (e.g., biomarker-heavy covariates in PGS004599). Main limitation: many candidates report only full-model metrics and heterogeneous endpoints/covariates, so cross-model metric comparability is imperfect; confidence is therefore moderate rather than high.

Direct-match psoriasis candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo=psoriasis). Among them, PGS001312 has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: Psoriasis; trait_reported: Psoriasis) and provides explicitly PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.69158; PGS-only R²=0.05226) with standard/basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and a large validation sample (n=67,425, European). Competing direct psoriasis models either (a) are time-to-event variants with slightly weaker metrics (PGS001313), (b) come from portability/framework-style studies with weaker/less comparable metrics (PGS001871/PGS002083 report partial-r only), or (c) focus on different endpoints such as severity/severe psoriasis rather than generic psoriasis status (PGS004315-317; PGS005307-312), reducing endpoint alignment for the generic target trait. Main limitation: the selected model is from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as often less reliable for external generalization than disease-focused multi-cohort scores; additionally, several other direct-match psoriasis scores lack directly comparable PRS-only metrics, preventing a higher-confidence best-in-class determination from the visible evidence.

Both candidates are direct matches to psoriatic arthritis by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported. PGS000342 is from a disease-focused publication explicitly evaluating a genetic risk score for diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis, which is supportive for endpoint fidelity relative to PGS001287, whose publication context is a pan-trait UK Biobank framework (“across 813 traits”) that domain guidance flags as systematically less reliable for external generalization. However, PGS000342 has limited and less PRS-comparable performance evidence (only a full-model AUROC 0.562 with unknown covariates and no PGS-only metrics), and uses only 11 variants, while PGS001287 reports explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.676 and PGS R2 0.0335) with basic covariates and larger validation. This creates meaningful competing evidence (endpoint-focused study vs stronger PRS-only metrics from a framework score), so the best choice is not unequivocal, lowering confidence and making the overall direct-match selection sub-optimal.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to pulmonary embolism at the concept level, but several are from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper ("Significant sparse polygenic risk scores across 813 traits in UK Biobank"; PGS001277/PGS001278/PGS001279/PGS001280), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly versus disease-focused studies. Among the EUR-evaluated, PE-specific options, PGS001280 has the cleanest endpoint alignment (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported both PE; not a PE+DVT composite) and shows comparable PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates 0.60765; PGS R2 0.01403) with basic covariates; its PRS-only R2 is below the provided EUR heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0052; liability h2=0.1090), so it passes the sanity check. However, confidence is limited because the best non-framework disease-focused candidate (PGS003861; Han Chinese PE GWAS) reports only a full-model AUROC (0.765) with unknown covariates and lacks PRS-only metrics, making cross-candidate performance comparison non-comparable; additionally, the newer EUR ICD10 I26 models (PGS004460/PGS004530) lack AUC/R2 and provide only modest ORs, leaving no clearly high-quality, well-characterized disease-focused EUR PRS in the visible evidence.

Direct-match candidates are present (pulmonary fibrosis / idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis). PGS001791 is preferred because its phenotype is a clinically specific direct match to the target spectrum (idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis) and it comes from a large multi-biobank development context (Global Biobank analyses) using a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant count, which domain guidance treats as structurally favorable versus sparse pan-trait framework scores. PGS001030 is an exact-label pulmonary fibrosis score but is from a known pan-trait sparse UKB framework ("across 813 traits"; 51 variants), which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused alternatives; its high full-model AUROC is likely covariate-driven given small incremental AUROC and modest PGS-only metrics. PGS004695 is also endpoint-aligned (incident idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis) and shows a strong HR (high vs low quintile), but it lacks PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and uses a small GWAS-hits SNP set, making it harder to compare directly. Remaining limitation: none of the candidates provides a clearly comparable, standalone PRS discrimination metric across studies (and PGS001791 lacks PGS-only AUROC), so the selection is supported mainly by endpoint fidelity + study/method structure rather than decisive head-to-head performance evidence.

All four candidates are direct matches to retinal detachment by trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, but they come from two framework-style UK Biobank papers ("across 813 traits" snpnet; "Portability of 245 polygenic scores"), which domain guidance flags as generally less reliable than disease-focused models; no disease-focused multi-cohort alternative is present here. Among the candidates, PGS001137 has the cleanest endpoint alignment (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both exactly "Retinal detachment") and provides explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.573 and PGS R2=0.00663) with only basic covariates; it also shows higher incremental AUROC (0.0185) than the closely related snpnet time-to-event composite endpoint model PGS000990. The main limitation is that all options are framework-derived and the observed PRS signal is modest (PGS-only R2 well below the local heritability ceiling), while the portability-framework models (PGS001833/PGS002040) lack PRS-only AUROC/R2 and report only partial-r, making cross-model comparison incomplete.

Direct-match rheumatoid arthritis candidates are present with coherent endpoint alignment (multiple models with trait_efo=rheumatoid arthritis and phenotyping_reported including “Rheumatoid arthritis”, “Seropositive RA”, and “Incident RA”). Among these, PGS004163 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) has strong within-context support: it is a direct RA model, uses an ensemble/multi-score method (a positive structural signal per domain_knowledge), and reports the strongest discrimination in the visible RA set with full-model AUROC 0.7469 and the highest reported R² (0.1376) alongside a strong OR (2.46). All four candidates are direct matches to sarcoidosis, but the evidence is limited and somewhat conflicted by phenotype mapping. PGS000922 and PGS000923 map to the sarcoidosis EFO term and report PRS-comparable metrics including PGS-only AUROC/R² plus full-model AUROC with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), making them the most directly comparable options. The two 2022 portability-framework models (PGS001872, PGS002084) have trait_efo listed as skin sarcoidosis and lack PRS-comparable AUROC/R² (only partial correlation), reducing endpoint alignment and comparability. Confidence is low because the top two candidates are from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (a known weaker archetype in the provided domain knowledge) and the remaining candidates have phenotype/metric limitations.

All five candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo = schizophrenia. Endpoint fidelity differentiates them: PGS000133/PGS000134/PGS000135/PGS000136 all report phenotyping_reported = Schizophrenia (aligned), while PGS002785—despite schizophrenia labeling—has phenotyping_reported = Cognitive function (Cognitive total), making it endpoint-misaligned for schizophrenia risk. All three candidates are direct matches to the target trait with consistent concept/endpoint fields (trait_efo = skin carcinoma in situ; phenotyping_reported = Carcinoma in situ of skin) and similar EUR-only training/development/evaluation context from the same publication family, so selection hinges mainly on the available performance/effect-size evidence. PGS000471 (lassosum) shows the strongest reported discrimination within this sibling set (full-model AUROC 0.569 vs 0.557 and 0.524), the highest Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (0.0255 vs 0.0154 and 0.00141), and the strongest effect sizes (OR per SD 1.401; top 1% vs rest OR 3.77), making it the best-supported direct-match choice given the visible metadata. Main limitation: none of the models report PRS-only (covariate-free) AUROC/R², so the reported AUROC values are full-model with basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs) and are not strictly comparable as standalone PRS metrics; this keeps confidence below High despite PGS000471’s consistent advantage across multiple reported metrics.

Direct-match candidates are present for sleep apnea, including multiple ExPRSweb “Sleep apnea” scores (PGS003204–PGS003218) and several obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) scores (PGS003479, PGS003857/PGS003858, PGS005219/PGS005220). The main limitation is that the reported AUROC is a full-model metric with BMI included as a covariate (and no PGS-only AUROC/R2 is provided), so the discrimination evidence is not directly comparable across models and may be covariate-influenced; additionally, ExPRSweb models are framework-derived and show near-null full-model AUROC (~0.49–0.53), but lack PRS-only metrics, making the overall direct-match selection less definitive.

Multiple direct-match candidates are present with consistent phenotype alignment to squamous cell carcinoma (e.g., PGS000120, PGS000460–PGS000468, PGS000731, PGS005209). Several newer UKB benchmarking/framework-style scores report PRS-only metrics or partial correlations, but domain guidance cautions these frameworks often underperform disease-focused models in external validation, and their reported metrics are not clearly superior here.

Direct-match candidates for the target concept (uterine cancer) are present, including exact/umbrella uterine cancer endpoints (PGS000541, PGS000542, PGS001795, PGS003740) and the clinically dominant subtype endometrial/uterine endometrial carcinoma (PGS000075, PGS000786, PGS002300, PGS002735-002737, PGS003381, PGS004244). Domain knowledge states endometrial carcinoma is the dominant subtype of uterine carcinoma (~90%), so endometrial-cancer-labeled models are acceptable direct matches. Among these, PGS003381 has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: uterine endometrial carcinoma), a genome-wide method (lassosum) with large variant count (529,365), and comparatively strong reported discrimination in its selected European validation (full-model AUROC 0.761; R² 0.11 with only age + PCs covariates). Competing exact-label uterine cancer models show weaker discrimination (e.g., PGS000541/PGS000542 AUROC ~0.57; PGS001795 AUROC 0.66 with very small PRS-only R² 0.001948), and PGS003740 lacks comparable AUC/R². Main limitation: PGS003381 does not report explicit PRS-only AUROC/R², so its AUROC/R² may be partially covariate-influenced and cross-study comparability is imperfect; confidence is therefore moderate rather than high.

All three candidates are direct trait matches by `trait_reported`/`trait_efo` (vitiligo), so selection hinges on endpoint fidelity (`phenotyping_reported`) and PRS-comparable performance evidence. PGS000738 has the most endpoint-faithful labeling (reported as vitiligo) and comes from a vitiligo-focused publication; it also provides a (weak but interpretable) pseudo R² (0.0386) that is below the provided EUR heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.1738), supporting metric plausibility. However, its `phenotyping_reported` field is inconsistent ('Red hair'), which materially lowers endpoint-fidelity confidence. PGS000760 has a clear endpoint mismatch (`phenotyping_reported`: anti-PD-L1 induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients), making it a weaker direct vitiligo PRS despite being labeled vitiligo and reporting HR=1.41. PGS001536 reports explicit PRS-only AUROC (0.6419) and PRS-only R² (0.0162) with basic covariates, but it is from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper and uses a time-to-event endpoint, both of which are warning signals in the provided domain guidance. Given these conflicts and metadata inconsistencies, a best pick is possible but not strongly supported, hence low confidence and a sub-optimal direct-match outcome.
